q1: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(FOLLOWEE) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW WHERE FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
q2: WITH FOLLOWEES AS ( SELECT FOLLOWEE, COUNT(*) AS NUM_FOLLOWED_BY FROM FOLLOW GROUP BY 1 ), FOLLOWERS AS ( SELECT FOLLOWER, COUNT(*) AS NUM_FOLLOWS FROM FOLLOW GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT F1.FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, F1.NUM_FOLLOWED_BY AS NUM FROM FOLLOWEES F1 INNER JOIN FOLLOWERS F2 ON F1.FOLLOWEE = F2.FOLLOWER ORDER BY 1 ASC

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 counts the number of followers for each followee that is also a follower, while Q2 counts the number of followers for each followee and the number of people each follower is following, and then joins these two counts on the followee.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where user A follows user B, and user B follows user A, but user C only follows user A. In this case, Q1 will count user A as following user B, while Q2 will not count user A as following user B because user B is not following user A.
